newsitem.title: USA: PSE&G seeks delay in consideration of alternatives.
newsitem.headline: PSE&G seeks delay in consideration of alternatives.

text.p: Public Service Electric and Gas Co said Monday it asked the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities to place the utility's proposed NJ Partners in Power Alternative Regulation Plan on inactive status pending completion of the board's Energy Master Plan.

"Many of the issues to be decided in the Energy Master Plan parallel the issues we have raised in our alternative regulation plan" announced in mid-January, the Public Service Enterprise Group Inc subsidiary pointed out.
The board expects to issue a draft plan this fall and make policy decisions by year end, the utility noted.
In July, the board issued a report on the Energy Master Plan saying such issues as industry restructuring, retail competition, and the treatment of transition costs must be addressed.
"It makes sense for the BPU to deal with the Energy Master Plan before it takes up the review of our alternative regulation plan," PSE&G explained.
Spokesman Neil Brown said the board had been considering its proposal in parallel with the utility's. Discovery on the PSE&G's proposal was just begining and no hearings had been scheduled, he noted.

The PSE&G statement pointed out the Master Plan proceeding will deliberate a number of issues with significant economic implications, including the future structure of New Jersey's electric energy delivery system and treatment of costs associated with the transition to a competitive energy marketplace.
The company said the issues and details of the master plan should be clarified and understood before proceeding with PSE&G's alternative regulation plan.
"It is important that the elements of our rate plan are in line with the direction of the Energy Master Plan which will define the structure of New Jersey's energy marketplace," it explained.
In its request filed Monday, PSE&G asked that, once the NJ Partners in Power plan is placed on inactive status, discovery proceedings and public hearings be held in abeyance.
